name: uade
desc: Play Amiga tunes through UAE emulation
why: Running Amiga tracker music through 68k CPU emulation is a strange and wonderful way to hear old chip-driven songs.

brief.what_it_is: UADE (Unix Amiga Delitracker Emulator) is a player for old Amiga tracker and chiptune music files on Unix-like systems. It runs the original Amiga player code for each format inside a 68k CPU emulator built on the UAE project, and it reimplements the Eagleplayer and Delitracker player APIs so those players can run outside AmigaOS. It takes Amiga music files as input and plays them as audio. The GitLab project page describes it as playing 200+ Amiga computer music formats. The homepage says it is designed to run from the command line or as a player plugin. The brew metadata lists three executables: uade123, bencat, and mod2ogg2.sh.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames UADE as a way to play old Amiga tunes on modern platforms. Its authors say the players built for the Eagleplayer and Delitracker ecosystems are reusable only because UADE makes them run on modern systems, and it builds on the UAE team's emulation work.
brief.how_it_works: Rather than reimplementing each format's parser, UADE emulates the Amiga's m68k code and runs the original player routines in that environment. A free implementation of the Eagleplayer and Delitracker APIs supplies the surrounding infrastructure. The homepage describes the design as a cmdline tool or a player plugin.
brief.install_notes: The brew metadata lists the executables uade123, bencat, and mod2ogg2.sh but shows no install steps. The homepage links to sources and binary packages for various distributions and platforms, and a version control repository and Matrix room for help. Nothing I fetched covered first-run configuration or runtime requirements.
brief.standout: Instead of decoding each tracker format, it runs the original Amiga player code under 68k CPU emulation, so the playback matches what the Amiga itself would produce. The project also keeps a reusable player ecosystem alive, which the homepage credits to the Eagleplayer and Delitracker authors.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage news lists UADE 3.05 released 2024-10-06, after 3.04 on 2024-09-28 and 3.03 in 2023-09-08. The page footer says 2020-07-22, which looks like a stale footer date. The GitLab project page shows it was created in July 2018. I did not check the last commit date.
brief.caveats: The license is inconsistent between sources. The homepage says GPL, while the GitLab project page says GNU LGPLv2.1. Check the source before relying on either. The homepage names Free/OpenBSD, GNU/Linux, Mac OS X (ppc), and AmigaOS/MorphOS as targets, and it does not say anything about Windows. I saw no commands in the README, so I could not verify usage. I did not read the full README because the GitLab page gave only a short summary.
quotes: UADE plays old Amiga tunes through UAE emulation and cloned m68k-assembler Eagleplayer API.
It is designed to be run on cmdline or as a player plugin.
UADE makes these players reusable on modern platforms.
